Active parameters vs total parameters
See the two entries in chapter 2.6. Active sets FLOPs per token; total sets memory.
Arithmetic intensity
FLOPs an operation performs ÷ bytes it must read and write. Compared with the GPU's ops:byte ratio to decide whether it is memory-bound or compute-bound.
BF16 (bfloat16)
A 16-bit float with FP32's 8 exponent bits and 7 mantissa bits: same range as FP32, less precision. The default weight format for serving.
BPE (byte-pair encoding)
A tokenizer training method that starts from bytes or characters and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token.
Causal mask
A mask that stops each token attending to later tokens, so a token's output depends only on itself and earlier tokens.
Chunked prefill
Splitting a long prompt's prefill into chunks that run in the same steps as other requests' decodes, so long prompts do not stall token output for everyone.
Compute-bound
An operation whose time is set by arithmetic speed (FLOP/s), not memory speed. Large-batch prefill is the main example.
Constrained decoding (structured output)
Masking the logits at each step so only tokens that keep the output valid for a grammar or JSON schema can be sampled.
Continuous batching
Scheduling at the level of single token steps: finished requests leave and new ones join the running batch at every step, instead of waiting for a whole batch to finish.
CUDA graph
A recorded sequence of GPU kernel launches that can be replayed with one call, removing per-kernel CPU launch overhead in decode.
Decode
The phase that makes output tokens one at a time, each step reading all weights and the KV cache. Usually memory-bound.
Disaggregated serving
Running prefill and decode on separate GPU pools and moving the KV cache between them, so each phase can be sized and batched for its own bottleneck.
Embedding
The learned vector for a token ID, looked up from the embedding table at the start of the model.
FlashAttention
An attention kernel that computes attention in tiles held in on-chip memory, never writing the full score matrix to HBM. Same result, far less memory traffic.
FP8
8-bit floating point (E4M3 or E5M2). Used for weights, activations or the KV cache on GPUs with FP8 tensor cores (Ada, Hopper, Blackwell).
GGUF
The single-file model format used by llama.cpp, holding weights (often quantized) and metadata such as the tokenizer and chat template.
Goodput
Throughput counted only for requests that meet their latency targets (SLOs).
GQA (grouped-query attention)
Attention where groups of query heads share one key head and one value head, which shrinks the KV cache by the group factor.
HBM (high-bandwidth memory)
The GPU's main memory. Its bandwidth (for example about 3.35 TB/s on an H100 SXM) sets the decode speed limit.
KV cache
Stored key and value vectors of every past token in every layer, so each new token step computes only the new token's keys and values.
LoRA
A fine-tuning method that trains two small low-rank matrices per adapted weight instead of the full weight. Serving engines can load many LoRA adapters over one base model.
MBU (model bandwidth utilization)
Achieved memory bandwidth ÷ peak bandwidth during decode. Measures how close decode gets to the memory floor.
MFU (model FLOPs utilization)
Achieved FLOP/s ÷ peak FLOP/s. Used mostly for prefill and training.
Memory-bound
An operation whose time is set by how fast bytes move from memory, not by arithmetic. Small-batch decode is the main example.
MLA (multi-head latent attention)
Attention that caches one small compressed latent vector per token per layer instead of full keys and values, then expands it when needed. Used by DeepSeek V2 and V3.
MoE (mixture of experts)
A model whose feed-forward layers hold many experts; a router sends each token to a few of them. Memory follows total parameters; compute follows active parameters.
NVFP4
NVIDIA's 4-bit floating-point format for Blackwell GPUs, with a scale factor per block of 16 values.
OpenAI-compatible API
An HTTP API that copies OpenAI's chat completions and completions endpoints, so the same client code works with vLLM, SGLang and other servers.
PagedAttention
Storing the KV cache in fixed-size blocks anywhere in GPU memory, with a block table per request, and an attention kernel that reads through the table. Removes most fragmentation.
Prefill
The phase that processes the whole prompt in one parallel pass and writes its KV cache. Usually compute-bound; sets TTFT.
Prefix caching
Keeping the KV blocks of earlier requests and reusing them when a new request starts with the same tokens, skipping their prefill.
Preemption
Pausing a running request when KV memory runs out, by freeing its blocks (recompute later) or copying them to CPU memory (swap).
Quantization
Storing weights, activations or the KV cache in fewer bits (for example INT8, FP8, INT4) to cut memory and bandwidth, at some accuracy risk.
Radix tree (prefix tree)
A tree keyed by token sequences. SGLang's RadixAttention uses it to find the longest cached prefix of a new request.
RMSNorm
A normalization layer that divides a vector by its root mean square and multiplies by learned gains. Used instead of LayerNorm in most current LLMs.
RoPE (rotary position embedding)
Encoding position by rotating each pair of query and key dimensions by an angle proportional to the token's position, so attention scores depend on relative distance.
Roofline
A plot of attainable FLOP/s against arithmetic intensity: a sloped memory roof and a flat compute roof meeting at the ops:byte ratio.
safetensors
A simple, safe file format for tensors (a JSON header plus raw bytes), the standard for Hugging Face model weights.
Sampling (temperature, top-k, top-p)
Picking the next token from the probability distribution. Temperature sharpens or flattens it; top-k keeps the k most likely tokens; top-p keeps the smallest set whose probabilities reach p.
Sliding-window attention
Attention where each token sees only the last W tokens, which caps that layer's KV cache at W tokens.
SLO (service level objective)
A target for a latency or availability metric, for example p95 TTFT under 500 ms.
Softmax
The function that turns a list of logits into probabilities: exponentiate each, then divide by the sum.
Speculative decoding
A cheap draft proposes several tokens; the big model checks them all in one pass and keeps the accepted ones. Output distribution is unchanged; latency drops when acceptance is high.
State space model (linear attention, Mamba)
A layer that keeps a fixed-size state per sequence instead of a growing KV cache. Constant memory and per-token cost; weaker exact recall.
Tensor parallelism
Splitting each weight matrix across GPUs so every GPU computes part of every layer, with all-reduce communication after each split layer.
Throughput
Tokens produced per second across all requests on a server or GPU.
Zero point
An offset stored with a quantization scale so that an asymmetric range of values (for example −0.2 to 1.5) maps onto the integer grid without wasting levels.
Per-channel and group-wise scales
One quantization scale per output channel, or per group of consecutive weights (for example 128). Smaller groups follow outliers better at the cost of storing more scales.
GPTQ

A post-training weight quantization method that rounds weights one column at a time and adjusts the remaining weights to compensate for each rounding error, using second-order information from calibration data.
AWQ (activation-aware weight quantization)
A weight-only quantization method that scales up the small share of weight channels that see large activations before rounding, protecting the weights that matter most.
SmoothQuant
Moves the difficulty of quantizing activations into the weights: divides activation outliers by a per-channel factor and multiplies the matching weights by it, so both can be stored in 8 bits.
MQA (multi-query attention)
Attention in which all query heads share one key head and one value head, shrinking the KV cache by the number of heads.
Online softmax
Computing softmax in one pass over blocks of scores by keeping a running maximum and running sum and rescaling earlier partial results. The basis of FlashAttention.
Flash-Decoding (split-KV attention)
Decode attention that splits the KV sequence into chunks processed in parallel and then merges the partial results, so one query can keep the whole GPU busy.
Attention sink
The first few tokens of a sequence, which receive large attention weights regardless of content. Keeping them makes sliding-window attention stable.
EAGLE
A speculative decoding drafter: a small head that predicts the next tokens from the target model's own hidden states.
MTP (multi-token prediction)
Extra prediction heads trained with the model to predict several future tokens; at inference they can serve as a built-in drafter.
KV offloading (tiered KV cache)
Keeping KV blocks that do not fit, or are idle, in CPU memory, local disk or a remote store, and loading them back instead of recomputing them.
Cache-aware routing
Sending a request to the replica most likely to hold its prefix in the KV cache, balanced against that replica's load.
Pipeline parallelism
Splitting a model by layers across GPUs or nodes; each stage passes activations to the next.
Expert parallelism
Placing different experts of a mixture-of-experts model on different GPUs and sending each token to the GPUs that hold its chosen experts.
Data parallelism
Running full copies of a model (or of some of its layers) on several GPUs, each serving different requests.
Context parallelism
Splitting one long sequence across GPUs so each holds part of its tokens and KV cache.
xPyD
Shorthand for a disaggregated deployment with x prefill workers and y decode workers.
KV eviction (H2O, SnapKV)
Dropping the KV entries of tokens that receive little attention, to bound memory at long context. Unlike paging, the dropped information is lost.
RULER
A long-context benchmark of synthetic retrieval, tracing and aggregation tasks at controlled lengths, used to measure the context a model really handles.
Ring attention
Context-parallel attention in which GPUs pass blocks of keys and values around a ring while each computes attention for its own queries.
SM (streaming multiprocessor)
The GPU's unit of execution: it holds tensor cores, registers and shared memory, and runs thread blocks.
Occupancy
The share of an SM's maximum resident warps that are actually resident. Enough occupancy hides memory latency; more is not always faster.
Tensor core
A GPU unit that multiplies small matrix tiles in one instruction, providing most of the GPU's FLOPs for matmuls.
Kernel fusion
Combining several operations into one GPU kernel so intermediate results stay on chip instead of making round trips through HBM.
Triton
A Python-embedded language and compiler for writing GPU kernels at the level of blocks of data rather than individual threads.
MIG (Multi-Instance GPU)
Partitioning one NVIDIA data-center GPU into isolated slices, each with its own memory and compute.
torch.compile
PyTorch's compiler: captures the model as a graph and generates fused kernels for it.
Piecewise CUDA graphs
Capturing CUDA graphs for the parts of a model step between operations that cannot be captured (such as some attention kernels), as vLLM does.
Tiling
Splitting a matmul or attention into tiles that fit in shared memory and registers, so each value loaded from HBM is reused many times.
Split-K
A matmul strategy that splits the reduction dimension across thread blocks and adds the partial results, used when the output is too small to keep the GPU busy.
Open-loop and closed-loop load

Open loop: requests arrive on a schedule (for example at a fixed rate) whatever the server does. Closed loop: a fixed number of clients each wait for a reply before sending again, which hides overload.
Cold start
The time from deciding to add a replica to it serving traffic: getting a machine, pulling the image, loading weights, compiling and warming up.
Readiness and liveness probes
Health checks: liveness asks whether the process should be restarted; readiness asks whether it can receive traffic now.
Graceful draining
Stopping new requests to a replica while letting in-flight ones finish before it shuts down.
Concurrency target
The number of simultaneous requests one replica should handle while meeting the SLO. Autoscalers scale on it.
Scale to zero
Removing all replicas of an idle deployment, accepting a cold start for the next request.
Power of two choices
A routing policy: pick two replicas at random and send the request to the less loaded one.
Erlang C
The queueing formula for c identical servers with random arrivals, used to estimate waiting time at a given utilization.
Reserved, on-demand and spot capacity
GPU purchasing models: committed blocks at a discount; pay-as-you-go up to a quota; discounted spare capacity that can be reclaimed at short notice.
Canary deployment
Sending a small share of traffic to a new version, watching its metrics, and raising the share in steps or rolling back.
Blue-green deployment
Running a full second fleet with the new version and switching all traffic at once.
histogram_quantile
The PromQL function that estimates a percentile from histogram buckets by linear interpolation inside the bucket that holds it.
DCGM (Data Center GPU Manager)
NVIDIA's tool for GPU health and performance metrics, exported to Prometheus with dcgm-exporter.
LeaderWorkerSet
A Kubernetes API that treats a leader pod and its worker pods as one replica, for models sharded across nodes.
TEE (trusted execution environment)
Hardware-protected execution whose memory the host cannot read, with attestation to prove what is running.
Context engineering
Designing what goes into a model's context, and in what order, for quality, latency and cache reuse.
Programmatic tool calling
The model writes code that calls tools inside a sandbox and returns only the processed result to the context.
MCP (Model Context Protocol)
An open standard for connecting models and agents to tools and data sources.
Xid error
An error code from the NVIDIA driver in the kernel log, identifying GPU faults such as memory errors or a GPU falling off the bus.
MTTF (mean time to failure)
Average time between failures; for a group of nodes, 1 ÷ (nodes × failure rate per node).
Retry budget
A limit on retries per request and across the fleet, so that a partial outage does not turn into a retry storm.
Cache salt
A per-tenant value mixed into prefix-cache block hashes so only requests with the same salt can share cached KV blocks.
Incident commander
The person who holds the overall state of an incident, assigns roles and makes decisions.
Pareto curve (throughput vs interactivity)
An engine's throughput per GPU plotted against tokens per second per user across concurrency levels; a curve above and to the right is better at every operating point.
DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
Preference tuning on chosen and rejected answer pairs with a classification loss against a frozen reference model; no reward model and no sampling during training.
GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)
An RL method that samples a group of answers per prompt and uses each answer's reward minus the group mean (divided by the spread) as its advantage, with no value model.
RLHF and RLVR
RL from human feedback (a reward model trained on human comparisons) and RL with verifiable rewards (automatic checks such as unit tests or exact maths answers).
Reward hacking
The policy finds outputs that score highly under the reward but are not what was wanted, such as padding answers to earn a length-correlated reward.
Overlong penalty
A reward term that penalizes answers beyond a length threshold, used to stop RL from inflating answer length.
Catastrophic forgetting
Loss of skills that are not in the fine-tuning data, such as general instruction following, after training on a narrow task.
NF4 and double quantization
QLoRA's 4-bit NormalFloat format for normally distributed weights, and the quantization of its block scales to cut their overhead to about 0.127 bits per parameter.
Multi-LoRA serving
Serving many LoRA adapters on one base model in the same batches, fetching adapters to the GPU as requests need them.
Train-inference mismatch
Differences between the probabilities a trainer computes and those the inference engine sampled with, from different kernels, templates or precision.
Thinking budget
A per-request cap on reasoning tokens, after which the engine forces the end of the thinking section.
Generation stall
A pause in ongoing decodes while a whole new prefill runs in one iteration; chunked prefill removes it.
Muon
An optimizer for hidden-layer weight matrices that orthogonalizes the momentum update with a few Newton-Schulz iterations.
Evolution strategies (ES)
Gradient-free optimization that evaluates a population of randomly perturbed models and moves toward the better ones; EGGROLL makes the perturbations low rank.
Slot mapping
The position of each token's keys and values in a paged KV cache: block table entry p // block size, offset p % block size.
Lightning indexer
A small, cheap scoring network in DeepSeek Sparse Attention that scores every earlier token (or compressed entry) for each query, so real attention runs only on the top-k. Can run in FP8 or FP4.
Redundant experts
Extra copies of frequently used MoE experts placed on other GPUs, so no single GPU becomes the straggler under expert parallelism. Placed by observed load (EPLB).
EPLB (expert-parallel load balancer)
DeepSeek's algorithm for choosing which experts to replicate and where: a hierarchical policy (expert groups to nodes, then within nodes) for prefill and a global policy for wide decode.
DeepEP

DeepSeek's library of all-to-all dispatch and combine kernels for expert parallelism over NVLink and RDMA. Version 1 had high-throughput (prefill) and low-latency (decode) kernels; version 2 unified them in one EPBuffer interface.
Data-parallel attention (attention DP)
Each GPU runs full attention for its own subset of requests and holds only their KV cache, while MoE layers use expert parallelism across the same GPUs. Avoids KV duplication for MLA.
Attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD)
Running attention and the feed-forward or MoE layers of the same model on separate GPU pools, passing activations between them each layer (Step-3, MegaScale-Infer).
Ping-pong pipelining
Splitting a batch into micro-batches that alternate between an attention pool and an expert pool so both stay busy, as in MegaScale-Infer.
Zero-computation expert
An MoE routing slot that returns its input unchanged at no cost, so the number of real experts (and active parameters) varies per token, as in LongCat-Flash.
DSpark

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's speculative decoding module: a three-block drafter that proposes five tokens, plus a confidence head whose predicted acceptance rates decide how many drafts each request verifies.
Confidence-scheduled verification
Choosing per request how many draft tokens to verify from their predicted acceptance probabilities and the engine's cost curve, instead of a fixed draft length.
Selective batching
Orca's technique of batching the operations that ignore sequence boundaries (linear layers over a flat token list) while running attention per request; the basis of continuous batching.
Delta rule
A linear-attention update that first reads what the state returns for a key and writes only the difference, so new information replaces old along that key. Gated DeltaNet adds a forgetting gate.
Lightning attention
MiniMax's blockwise linear attention, which passes the running state between blocks of tokens; used in 7 of every 8 layers of MiniMax-01 and M1.
QK-Clip
Kimi K2's fix for Muon training instability: after each update, rescale the query and key projection weights so attention logits stay bounded (MuonClip).
Cascade attention (shared-prefix attention)
Computing attention over a prefix shared by many sequences once per decode step, with all their queries in one matrix product, then merging with per-sequence suffix attention (Hydragen).
Wide-EP
Expert parallelism over a large group (for example 64 to 128 GPUs in one supernode) for decode, so each expert sees enough tokens and each GPU reads fewer expert weights.
VE/prefill/decode disaggregation (EPD)
Running the vision encoder, prefill and decode of a multimodal model as three separately scaled pools.
